### Diagnosis

The current bug report points out that `ExtendedMessageFormat` doesn't override the `equals(Object)` method inherited from `MessageFormat`. This can lead to equality comparisons ignoring the identity of the subclass and only considering the identity of the superclass.

Looking at the test case `testEqualsHashcode`, it tries to test the equality between two `ExtendedMessageFormat` objects with different configurations. The test involves creating `ExtendedMessageFormat` instances with different patterns and registries to check if their hash codes are equal or not.

In the test case:
- Two `ExtendedMessageFormat` instances are created with the same pattern and registry, which should make them equal.
- Another instance is created with a different class (`OtherExtendedMessageFormat`), which should make it unequal.
- Additional instances are created with different patterns or registries to test inequality based on these differences.

The failure observed in the test execution might be due to the missing implementation of the `equals(Object)` method in `ExtendedMessageFormat`, leading to incorrect equality comparison results.

Looking at the code snippet of the `ExtendedMessageFormat` constructor, it doesn't include an explicit implementation of the `equals(Object)` method. This aligns with the reported issue of not overriding the method.

Additionally, the `LowerCaseFormatFactory` and `UpperCaseFormatFactory` classes are mentioned in the test as components of the format registry. These classes seem to provide formats based on case transformations. Their implementations are not shown directly, but they are used in creating the format registries for testing.

### Potential Fix Locations
- `org.apache.commons.lang3.text.ExtendedMessageFormat.equals(java.lang.Object)`
- Implement `equals(Object)` method in `org.apache.commons.lang3.text.ExtendedMessageFormat` class.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
